conventions.convention: AC is assumed. The projective decomposition theorem concerns projective morphisms between complex projective varieties with smooth source of pure complex dimension n; its initial coefficient field is Q.

K = Rf_*Q_X[n], P_b = perverse H^b(K), and F_bH^q is the image induced by perverse truncation at b. The induction orders (r(f), dim f(X)) lexicographically with defect primary; r(f) = max_i(2i + dim{y: dim f⁻¹(y)=i} − n).

η is a very ample source class and L is the pullback of a very ample target line class. Double primitives lie in H_{−i}^{n−i−j}; their form is (−1)^{t(t−1)/2}∫η^iL^ju∧v, t=n−i−j, with positivity Q_t(Cu, conjugate(u))>0 and C acting by i^{p−q}. Forms and primitive kernels are defined on canonical graded groups.

The centered increasing filtration W satisfies L(W_a)⊆W_{a−2} and L^a: Gr_a^W→Gr_{−a}^W is an isomorphism. The middle limit uses real cohomology and L+εη Kähler for every ε>0, together with the explicit hypotheses (a)–(c).

For a closed inclusion i with open complement j, A = perverse H^0(i^!P), B = perverse H^0(i^*P), and α:A→B is induced by the canonical supported subobject and quotient maps. The criterion is an iff and does not itself establish invertibility for projective direct images.
Characteristic-zero coefficient fields need not embed in C. Scalar extension uses semisimplicity of the complexifications of the rational IC local systems, not preservation of rational simplicity.
On a point, the perverse t-structure is the ordinary cohomological t-structure. Rf_*k[n] for P^n has nonzero degrees −n, −n+2, …, n and splitting ⊕_{j=0}^n k[n−2j].

load_bearing.statement: For a projective morphism of complex projective varieties with smooth connected source, very ample source class η and pulled-back very ample target class L, if the stated package holds for all smooth connected projective-source maps of lexicographically smaller pair (r,m), with r primary, then it holds for f. The package includes relative η hard Lefschetz, finite normalized perverse splitting, perverse semisimplicity with semisimple complexified IC local systems, target graded hard Lefschetz, pure Hodge graded groups, and polarized orthogonal double primitive decomposition. The image-dimension-zero base comes from absolute polarized Hodge theory and finite linear algebra; finite disconnected smooth sources are handled componentwise.

Under AC, the stated smooth-projective and Kähler hypotheses, and hypotheses (a)–(c), set D=ker(L:H^n→H^{n+2}), R=D∩W_{−1}H^n and M=η ker(L:H^{n−2}→H^n). The primitive limit Λ exists as a Hodge subspace, equals D∩⋂_{j≥1}(η^j ker L^j)⊥, and D=Λ ⊥⊕ M. The Poincaré radical on D is R; the classical degree-n signed form polarizes Λ/(Λ∩R), hence every Hodge subspace of D/R orthogonal to the image of M.

Assume inherited AC. For a closed complex algebraic inclusion i:Z→Y with open complement j and an ordinary constructible perverse sheaf P over a characteristic-zero field, the natural map α:perverse H^0(i^!P)→perverse H^0(i^*P) is an isomorphism if and only if P≃i_*A⊕j_{!*}j^*P. The supported subobject and quotient are maximal, and their composite is i_*α.

Assume inherited AC. For a projective morphism f:X→Y of complex projective varieties with X smooth of pure dimension n and η the first Chern class of an ample line bundle on X, η^i:perverse H^{−i}K→perverse H^iK is an isomorphism for every i≥0, where K=Rf_*Q_X[n]. K has a finite perverse splitting; each perverse cohomology object is a finite sum of IC objects of simple rational local systems whose complexifications are semisimple.

Assume inherited AC. For a projective morphism f:X→Y of complex projective varieties, X smooth of pure dimension n, and any characteristic-zero field k, Rf_*k_X[n] is a finite direct sum of shifts of simple perverse sheaves. Equivalently, all its perverse cohomology objects are semisimple and it splits into their shifted sum. No embedding k→C is required.

concerns.concern: The embedded construction texts retain stale assembly and ownership prose. Construction D says its stages 'would supply all primitive polarizations' and calls the source Thom/Gysin comparison 'pending', although Construction A already supplies that comparison and Construction E completes the middle inputs. Construction E likewise says refined fibre intersection and the moving family 'remain required components', although Constructions F–H follow in this same item. These passages obscure which obligations are discharged locally; this is a presentation concern, not a missing argument identified in the assembled proof.

seams_checked.note: The induction preserves the affine exactness directions, universal weak-Lefschetz indices and maximal pullback assertions. Strict source-defect decrease is used only for positive defect; the zero-defect boundary is separate.

Uses the ordinary analytic constructible category, its coherent proper exchanges and trace, smooth complex orientation and ordinary perverse recollement. No coherent-sheaf trace or quotient-stack normalization is substituted.

The cited Ext theorem is used in Remarks to identify the same ordinary scalar-extension deduction. The coefficient proof relies on the ordinary six-operation and perverse suppliers and does not infer semisimplicity from equivariant Ext finiteness.

Construction H constructs a smooth projective family over a smooth quasiprojective open and a genuine quotient of its Gauss–Manin local system. Dense-open fundamental-group surjectivity extends semisimplicity. Arbitrary analytic variations are not covered.

The abstract splitting is finite and noncanonical. Canonical primitive projectors come from the graded abelian-category lemma; no stronger primitive-compatible global lift is attributed to the splitting supplier. Centered-filtration shifts agree.

Uses absolute Hodge theory, real Kähler hard Lefschetz and classical signed primitive positivity. Relative and nonmiddle assertions are proved in the induction before the middle limit. The Weil-operator placement and degree sign are preserved.

Construction F applies the actual-image equality to smooth U′⊂X and proper fibre Z→U′. It retains the class-map Tate twist, then uses the untwisted pure image and previously proved Hodge perverse filtration.

The quiver corollary quotes the compact smooth-source theorem faithfully in F10. Proof 3.1 applies it to smooth projective compactifications of the finite Grassmannian models with source shift d_ν+s_N, then restricts to the open chart. It does not apply the theorem directly to the noncompact incidence source or assume semismallness.
